title: MWC Force writer contract
description: First-class contract for the Force (mwcforce) consult app. Force is NOT a GHL workflow and NOT a custom_code action. Force UPDATES an existing Sales opportunity via the public GHL API, then POSTs GHL_WF05_WEBHOOK_URL so native WF-05 routes. Force never creates a contact, appointment, or opportunity. Native GHL stays the law of the messaging graph. This spec lives beside the per-workflow specs in /to-be and is enumerable by extract-diff and the planning site. Nothing here publishes.

id.description: Stable id. There is exactly one Force writer contract.

role.description: Free-form description of what Force is and is not (consult app, not a workflow, not custom_code, updates existing opp via public API).

canonical_slugs.description: The three canonical clinic slugs Force will adopt when mwc-force / mwc-admin cut over. Do not invent additional clinics.

field.description: Field slug Force is the sole writer of on the target object.

on.description: Which object this field lives on. Force writes on the Opportunity by default; a small set of consult-notes / how-heard / referred-by / PCC / provider fields live on the Contact today and are noted explicitly.

purpose.description: One-line reason Force writes this field.

gated_by.description: Optional gating condition (for example "only when sale_outcome=SOLD" or "only when sale_outcome=AD").

writes.description: Fields Force is the sole writer of. Everything else on the opp must not be written by Force.

field.description: Field slug or field family Force must never write.

owner.description: Who does write this field (for example "native GHL workflow", "WF-01", "WF-06", "WF-11", "Curve (TBD)", or "nobody yet").

reason.description: Why Force is not the writer here.

does_not_write.description: Explicit non-writes. Everything Force must leave alone.

sale_outcome.description: SOLD, AD (Advise & Decline), MUT (must-follow-up), MAR (marketing / disqualified). Only Force writes this.

sales_pipeline_stages.description: The only stages Force may move an opportunity through. Force is the sole stage-mover on Sales Lead to Close. Workflows never move stages.

ad_reason.description: Required set for the ad_reason enumeration when sale_outcome=AD. Values are consult-app specific (Force owns the vocabulary).

enums.description: All enumerations Force writes. Any drift here is a contract violation.

target.description: Downstream system that Force pokes via webhook. WF-05 is the native GHL inbound-webhook router. Curve is the conversion-events endpoint at curvecompliance.com.

when.description: The sale_outcome values that fire the webhook. MAR does not fire. Force fires WF-05 on SOLD | AD | MUT and fires Curve on SOLD only (the SOLD conversion event).

url_env.description: Environment variable name in Force config that carries the endpoint URL. The URL itself is not stored in this repo; do not invent it (WF-05 URL is UI-only on the draft; Curve URL is provided by Curve at cutover).

event.description: Optional. Used only for Curve entries; names the locked conversion event this fire represents.

notes.description: Free-form notes on the webhook contract (idempotency stamp, retries, payload ownership). Do not invent Curve payload / field names in this repo.

fires.description: Hand-offs Force triggers after it writes. Native WF-05 routing and the Curve SOLD conversion event.

owner.description: Owning system for conversion events (Curve Compliance).

writer.description: System that POSTs the event to Curve. GHL workflows never POST to Curve.

on.description: Trigger point for this event (for example "contact create (WF-01 path)", "appointment created", "consult SOLD (Force + dollars)").

ghl_role.description: One-line statement of what GHL does and does not do here. GHL workflows do not POST to Curve and do not fire CAPI. WF-13 stays dropped.

conversion_events.description: Locked Curve conversion-events contract. Native GHL is not in this path.

system.description: System going live at this step (for example "Curve Compliance (curvecompliance.com)" or "New GHL folder").

when.description: Free-form target timing (for example "target next week", "after Curve is live"). Do not encode absolute dates that need re-editing.

note.description: One-line lock note for this step.

cutover_sequence.description: Cutover order. Curve goes first; the new GHL folder publishes after Curve is live. This repo never publishes.

keeps.description: Coarse ops signals GHL still tracks (for example "next-lander vs wordpress-form", "clinic slug").

drops_to_curve.description: Attribution facets that live in Curve, not in GHL (for example UTM, gclid, fbc, fbp, wbraid, gbraid).

ghl_source_scope.description: Scope split between GHL (coarse ops source) and Curve (attribution).

statement.description: One-line statement of the native-GHL-only rule.

must_not.description: Bullet list of what Force must not do (no custom_code, no new Supabase, no contact/appointment/opportunity creation, no attribution writes, no publish).

native_ghl_rule.description: The law that stays: native GHL only, Force never creates identity objects, and Force never publishes.

live_with_canonical_slugs.description: True once mwc-force / mwc-admin adopt richmond | virginia-beach | newport-news end-to-end. Today: false.

publishes.description: Nothing in this repo publishes. Locked to false.

notes.description: Free-form notes: attribution redesign hole, Curve Compliance ownership TBD, references to related SPEC sections.
